steps.text: Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in quinoa and allow to toast for 2 to 3 minutes, then add chicken broth, soy sauce, ginger and garlic. Increase heat and bring to a boil. Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer until all liquid has been absorbed, 25 to 30 minutes. Fluff quinoa with fork and top with green onions before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Quinoa with Asian Flavors
raw_recipe.description: Here’s an Asian twist to making quinoa. What a little ginger, garlic, and soy sauce can do to update your favorite side dish!
raw_recipe.name: Quinoa with Asian Flavors

recipeInstructions.text: Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in quinoa and allow to toast for 2 to 3 minutes, then add chicken broth, soy sauce, ginger and garlic. Increase heat and bring to a boil. Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer until all liquid has been absorbed, 25 to 30 minutes. Fluff quinoa with fork and top with green onions before serving.

review.reviewBody: I strongly recommend to rinse quinoa thoroughly before toasting it a little to remove its natural defense of bitterness & proceed w/the recipe.

This was my first time cooking quinoa. It was OK. I followed the recipe, and I typically love those flavors. However, it seemed like something was missing. One of the readers mentioned sesame oil (maybe toasted sesame seeds would be good, too) and that seems like it might improve the flavor. I liked the texture and the green onions. I think this has potential with some modifications.

So, I have revised my rating to four stars. Yesterday, using the leftover quinoa, I made "fried rice" with it as another reviewer suggested. In my wok, I sauteed thinly sliced carrot, minced garlic, and diced onion in olive oil for about five minutes, then I added the cold quinoa (I estimate it was about 2.5 cups leftover), cut-up asparagus (also leftover from the night before), a dash of Asian Perfect Pinch (McCormick), and more low-sodium soy sauce (about 2 T). After another five minutes, I pushed the quinoa mixture to the side and scrambled an egg. Mixing in the egg, I added leftover diced chicken and cooked the mixture through (another five minutes). Serving, I topped each bowl with green onions and a splash of soy sauce. It was fantastic!

This was a great start... I added a head of broccoli, 1/2 a red bell pepper, 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes and served with 3/4 lb of chicken I cooked seperately. I tossed the broccoli, pre-cooked chicken and red bell pepper in after 20 minutes and the veggies were perfectly done, not soggy! The recipe was a bit salty for my tastes; next time I will try 1 cup chicken broth, 1 cup water to reduce the sodium while keeping the soy sauce flavor.

Super delish, easy weekday meal! However, we definitely added half the soy sauce it calls for, about 3 times the garlic and also about 1-2 tablespoons of ginger. AND definitely add steamed broccoli! I just threw some chopped broccoli over the quinoa mixture with a little extra water as it finished cooking in the pan. This is really good stuff!

This was my first time trying Quinoa. I followed some of the other suggestions and added carrots, celery, peas, onions, and green onions that I cooked separately and added to the quinoa in the last 5 minutes. I also reduced the soy sauce even though I was using low salt soy sauce. Everyone loved it. I made it along with the slow cooker Mongolian Beef from this web site. That was also good. I messed up and added a little too much fresh ginger in it but still liked it. I steamed some fresh sugar snap peas to round out the meal. I will be making both recipes again!!

This is the best simple Quinoa recipe I have found so far, I did alter it a bit though. I used low sodium soy sauce, used two tablespoons grated fresh ginger. And for the onion (because I didn't have any green onions at the time) I used 1 tablespoon minced yellow onion and added it with the broth and other ingredients, then topped with crushed parsley. It was delicious as a healthy snack as well as a sidedish.

This is a fantastic quinoa recipe. I follow the ingredients exactly except for the last 5 minutes, I throw in a cup of shelled edamame and and a cup diced green onion. I save out half of the green tops of the onion to add raw before chowing down! The first night I eat it hot, but it is even better the next day cold for lunch! It is similar to couscous only better. Great flavors!
Use a tiny bit of toasted sesame oil, add extra ginger, a few chopped carrots, a few finely chopped broccoli florets, don't add soy sauce while cooking. Add sparingly after cooked.

Just made this for lunch and it was awesome. I reduced the soy sauce to 1 TB and increased the garlic and ginger (1 small bulb, or about a dozen cloves and 1/4 minced fresh ginger). I think that the cooking time directed may be too long. My quinoa seemed done about 10 minutes sooner than described in the recipe. Over cooking quinoa ruins the texture. It becomes mushy and loses the mild crunchiness it has when cooked until the spirals start showing on the kernels.

I was so surprised by how good this recipe is! I used 1/2 tb spoon of dark soy sauce and 1 1/2 tb of light soy sauce. I added silced carrots with the rice. When everything was ready I added pre-cooked cubed chicken and green beens. It was so so good! Perfect for a weeknight dinner.

I liked this dish. It's a perfect accompaniment if you desire a side dish with Asian flare. My only complaint is a subliminal bitterness in the background. Now, I see another rater recommended rinsing the quinoa first (before toasting it) to remove the bitterness. Dang it. I didn't know this! I wish the recipe included rinsing the quinoa in the instructions. Nevertheless, it's a good recipe and I will absolutely make it again (but I'll rinse the quinoa next time :)
Really good and easy to make. I added a few chopped peppers to it.
Loved it just as published. Will make it again.
Big hit with my family. Used one cup water + one cup broth to cut down on salt.

Love this recipe. Made it several times now, first time was over dark greens & topped w/ salmon & mandarin orange slices. Most recently topped with bean sprout stir-fry & spicy baked tofu. Every time is delicious!
I found it way too salty. I would use less soy sauce if I made it again.
I have made this twice, the second time I omitted the garlic (husband cannot eat it anymore). All I tasted was soy sauce. I was not a fan, probably won't make it again.
Too salty! Will make again but with less soy sauce.

I've made quinoa for a while now and always thinking ways of adding flavor to it. Great recipe overall. I agree with other reviews regarding soy sauce, I suggest cutting down the amount of soy sauce so it won't be too salty. I enjoy turmeric and added just a pinch, turned out great!
Way way to salty. I couldn't taste any other flavors over the salt. I think next time I'll half the soy and see how it goes. Still have two stars because I think the flavor mix has potential
